items.note: CHI system paper: InspirationGraph, a structured text-to-image ideation tool for novice product designers, tested in a 24-person user study; the abstract names no comparison condition and reports divergent thinking and cognitive load, so whether a baseline arm and output scoring exist needs the full text (below 50 participants in any case).

Pre-registered random-assignment experiments: practice writing cover letters with an AI tool versus alone, googling examples, or human editor feedback, then no-AI writing tests scored for quality; after_ai design, but the outcome is cover-letter writing quality, not creativity, so the next stage should check whether the task meets the creative-task boundary; N not stated in the abstract.

Mainly a model study of data-augmented LLM research ideation (climate negotiation), plus a human study where researchers proposed ideas with or without LLM-generated ideas and validation, and supported ideas were rated higher in quality; N and assignment not stated.

Three-arm randomized experiment (900 randomized, 659 analyzed): self-generation-first AI workflow, direct-adoption AI workflow, or no AI for an argumentative essay, then an unaided parallel essay; blind raters scored reasoning quality, idea diversity, and originality (after_ai; abstract reports only the reasoning effect).

Participants sketched abstract concepts before and after GPT-4 verbal or visual inspiration; sketches scored by neural-network semantic distance, uniqueness, and human and GPT-4 creativity ratings; compares two AI configurations, no no-AI arm stated; abstract from OpenAlex (CogSci 2025, DOI 10.48448/wd46-dd26), N and assignment not stated.

Quasi-experiment in a design thinking course: 65 students used a generative-AI-enhanced collaborative whiteboard or a conventional platform; pre/post tests of creativity and critical thinking plus engagement; whether the creativity test scores the project output or a separate test needs checking.

iDesignGPT multi-agent LLM framework for conceptual engineering design, benchmarked against GPT-4o and DeepSeek-r1 on outputs, plus two controlled user studies (search notes: n = 11 and n = 37 across human-only and AI workflows) that the abstract describes only through reception and mental demand; output creativity of human participants likely not scored, and both studies are under 50.

150 undergraduates wrote collaboratively under five conditions (human-human, or computer or robot partner driven by a high- or low-creativity LLM); originality, imagery, voice, and semantic flow scored by experts and computational measures; allocation procedure not stated.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC, web search all failed); title and search snippets suggest an AIGC-based design method raised novelty and elaboration of students' design outcomes, but design, comparison group, and N are unknown.

Applies UTAUT and AHP to rate Stable Diffusion and Midjourney against traditional methods on creativity, aesthetics, practicality, and feasibility in interior design education; looks like an acceptance survey and expert weighting (likely out as self-report or perception), kept only because Ozkan 2026 includes it in a creativity meta-analysis, so the full text should confirm whether any student outputs are compared.
